title: Lightning triage + cut-plan for sprint 21
body:
Context:
Quick workshop-style grooming to force decisions for Sprint 21 intake. Goal: surface the minimal set of console changes we can commit to ship in a 2-week cadence that move observability and routing UX forward without over-scoping backend work.

Workshop approach (lightning):
- 45m timebox. Each ticket gets 3 min: dev + PM quick read, 1–2 clarifying questions, vote (keep/cut/park).
- Output: Cut-plan with three buckets: ship-this-sprint (green), defer-but-keep-on-deck (amber), park/icebox (red).
- Emphasis: Remove surface-level polish items that depend on infra changes outside our control (routing, quota refactor).

Scope guide (how we judged):
- Latency-first: anything that improves triage or route selection observable in the console without infra rollout = higher priority.
- Customer-impact: quick wins for Dedicated customers and top 5 hosted API customers.
- Dev-effort: prefer items estimated <= 3 dev-days.
- Risk: features requiring DB schema changes or multi-service coordinated deploys -> defer.

Triage summary (tickets reviewed):
- RW-1283: route-fallback-visibility (owner: Marco) — current state: console shows generic 503 with no fallback metadata.
  - Decision: keep for sprint (green). Rationale: small UI change + existing API already surfaces fallback details.
  - Acceptance criteria: show fallback model id, elapsed time, and link to runtime trace. Wireframe notes: add a small inline pill with tooltip. Est: 2d.
- RW-1341: model-rollout-progress-bar (owner: Riya) — current: no progress indicator during canary. Backend needs progress endpoint.
  - Decision: defer (amber). Rationale: backend work out of scope for 2w; schedule for next cycle once RW-1390 (rollout API) lands.
- RW-1402: token-cost-breakdown-popover (owner: Elena) — current: token cost shown as single number, customers ask for per-token-type breakdown.
  - Decision: keep (green) but scope-moderate. Rationale: frontend only if metrics API returns per-type. Need quick backend stub. Est: 3d frontend + 1d infra stub. Contingency: if infra not ready, show placeholder with CTA linking to cost docs.
- RW-1428: compact-route-list-view (owner: Samir) — request to add compact table with inline controls.
  - Decision: park (red). Rationale: visual polish not critical; there are accessibility concerns requiring design time. Re-scope for later sprint.
- RW-1455: quick-search-autocomplete (owner: Avery) — console search needs fuzzy autocomplete for routes/models.
  - Decision: keep (green) but minimal MVP: prefix search + debounce. Est: 2d. Integrations: use existing search index; no new infra.

Wireframe/UX notes (quick sketches described as bullets):
- Fallback pill: small rounded rectangle, muted-red border for fallback; text: "fallback: redwood-small-v2" with hover tooltip listing reason and trace link. Place at top-right of request detail header.
- Progress bar: horizontal, thin 6px, color stops for canary vs stable. If backend returns percent null -> show dotted pulse placeholder + small "progress unavailable" tooltip.
- Token breakdown popover: triggered from cost number. Two-column layout: token-type | cost; footer: link to cost docs and button "Export last 7d". Mobile: stacked rows.

Cut-plan (final buckets):
- Ship this sprint (green): RW-1283, RW-1402 (frontend fallback path if infra ready), RW-1455.
- Defer (amber): RW-1341 (wait for RW-1390), RW-1490 (quota UI refactor — depends on rate-limiter change).
- Park (red): RW-1428, RW-1512 (console theme polish), RW-1530 (drag reorder routes)

Sprint assignments & owners (provisional):
- Marco: RW-1283 + testing assistance on fallback trace links.
- Elena: RW-1402 frontend + liaise with infra (Vikram) for per-token metrics.
- Avery: RW-1455 search MVP + product QA.
- Riya: unblock RW-1341 by tracking RW-1390 timeline; if RW-1390 slips, reassign RW-1341 to next sprint.

Blockers & mitigation:
- Infra: RW-1390 (rollout API) ETA uncertain. Mitigation: build frontend to degrade gracefully when endpoint missing (placeholder + CTA).
- Metrics: per-token-metrics endpoint currently gated by infra work item METR-22. Ask infra to expose a stubed endpoint for staging.
- Design hours: small wireframes needed for fallback pill and token popover. Request 1.5 designer days this sprint.

Open questions (to resolve in sync):
- Should fallback pill be dismissible? (UX)
- Metrics: can we contract a minimal staging API from infra or is a feature-flagged mock required?
- Search: fuzzy vs prefix — product tilt suggested fuzzy, but more infra cost. Vote: prefix for MVP.

Deliverables by EOD sprint planning meeting:
- Final cut-list document posted to Confluence + link in sprint description.
- PR template: include a small checklist: design screenshot, e2e for request detail, telemetry event added.
- QA plan: 3 smoke tests: (1) fallback pill shows on fallback responses; (2) token breakdown popover opens and exports csv; (3) search returns expected prefix matches.

Action items (owner -> task):
- Avery -> create RW tickets for UI stubs for fallback pill and token popover (if RW-1402 not sufficient).
- Marco -> implement RW-1283 UI and add trace-link telemetry.
- Elena -> coordinate with Vikram to get a staging per-token endpoint by 2026-08-05.
- Samir -> move compact-route visual polish to backlog with acceptance criteria and a11y notes.

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal):
- Consider a small toggle in user prefs to collapse non-critical logs in request view (could reduce noise).
- If rollout progress bar is delayed, we can show a lightweight heatmap of request durations per-version as interim UX.

Links / references used during workshop:
- Slack thread: #console-triage (link: slack://channel?team=T123&id=C987654)
- Confluence: Canary routing playbook (see linked_artifacts)
- Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/412 (progress bar spike experiment)

Final note: this doc is intentionally terse — treat as the single source for sprint 21 cut decisions for console work. Update the Confluence summary with final green items and link to sprint board before planning starts.
